description: Input — the field box, and only the box. The root is a WRAPPER (an <input> cannot contain children — icons live inside the field), with the native control reset flat inside; states read through it via :has(). THE CLASSIC EDS FIELD (the EDS 1.0 identity, restored v0.6.0 from mock 345:1023): bg-input fill, square corners, and a thin bottom border that carries the states — border-neutral-medium at rest. xs-STRETCHED inset (a field is a stretched box; converges vertically with md-squished while the horizontal inset drops to xs — the field hugs its text). Height is never stated: inset × 2 + cap(value) resolves to 24 / 36 / 44. The assembled field is a COMPOSITION — see compositions/text-field.json.
notes: v0.4.0 (Victor 2026-08-31): the BOXED field replaces EDS 1.0's underline — this redesign has real provenance (the previous team's mocks, continued by the current team), unlike the tab/banner redesigns we declined. Resting border is MEDIUM (Victor's call — a field is interactive; the visible affordance matches the mocks). States re-point the border: hover strong, :user-invalid danger-strong, disabled border-disabled; focus stays the ring (it REPLACES the border outline, same property). FIELDS SIT ON SURFACES, never the canvas (Victor's rule — and the box makes it moot in practice: the border separates the field from any backdrop). NOTE the team's border tokens now live in a third parallel system (non-interactive neutral muted/default/emphasis → primitive steps 4/7/9; interactive → 4/5/7; scale unidentified) — we stay on the semantic border ladder. One contract per box (Victor, 2026-08-29): EDS 1.0's drawback was designers assembling fields from parts; the fix is shipping BOTH the part and the composition. Validation is the platform's truth: invalid lowers to :has(:user-invalid) (matches only after user interaction — h/t Oddbjørn's design-system-css input). Icon slots per the EDS 2.0 Lab mockup (Text Input, 715:90251); REFUSED from that mockup for now: unit prefix/suffix, meta text, required marker (composition-level), warning/success validation tones (scoping list). Baseline-grid label alignment: recorded as an open idea, not built — Victor: labels are scanned, not read, 'I can't defend it', but shared form rhythm pleases. The disabled underline keeps its resting step. Placeholder ink has its own channel; Figma refuses it. v0.5.0 (2026-09-04): placeholder ink gets its own concept token — text-placeholder, disabled's rung under an honest name (Victor had hand-bound text-disabled: 'works, but looks disabled'; Lc 30 floor beside the affordance icon). Figma disposition placeholder ink REFUSED → LOWERED: the canvas component presents the EMPTY field, value text wears the placeholder ink; typed-text ink stays CSS-only. v0.6.0 (2026-09-05, Victor, from his mock 345:1023): BACK TO THE EDS 1.0 FIELD — square corners, filled bg-input, a thin bottom border (medium at rest, strong on hover, danger-strong invalid, border-disabled disabled). The v0.4.0 boxed look is retired here; the classic underline field is the EDS identity. v0.7.0 (2026-09-05, Victor, from the Figma review): THE VALUE FILLS — the spare inline space belongs to the text, so the trailing icon pins to the end while the leading icon keeps the normal icon gap (no nested wrapper groups: one FILL on the value is the whole mechanism, and it is what the CSS twin always did — flex: 1 1 auto on the control, fixed gaps both sides). The Figma set gets a 256 demo edge (the field's natural width, mock 345:1023; canvas convenience — instances resize freely).
